title: First halt in a padded run
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean tape symbols, and state set $S$. For a Boolean input word $x$, a configuration $c$, and $t\in\mathbb{N}$, suppose $c$ is live and the configuration reached after $t$ steps is halted. Then there is a time $u$ with $0<u\le t$ such that every configuration at time $v<u$ is live, and the configuration at time $u$ equals the one at time $t$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a $k$-work-tape Turing machine over Boolean symbols with states in $S$
The run from $c$ is halted at time $t$
replaced: Let a machine run from a live configuration to a halted configuration in $t$ steps. Then there is a strictly positive time $u \le t$ at which the run first halts, and the configuration at $u$ equals the configuration at $t$; padding by absorbed halted steps changes no endpoint field.
